'''''Rhodobryum roseum''''', commonly known as '''rose moss''', is a species of moss of the subclass [[Bryidae]] and family [[Bryaceae]], found throughout most of the world in woods or sheltered grassy places. It rarely forms [[sporophyte]]s and spore cases, and primarily reproduces vegetatively by [[stolons]], horizontal stems that root at the nodes, resulting in populations of plants that are sterile or only female.<ref name="britannica">{{cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/plant/rose-moss-Rhodobryum-roseum|title=Rose moss | plant, Rhodobryum roseum|website=Britannica.com|access-date=2018-04-14}}</ref>

==Description==
This species forms characteristic rosettes of leaves at the ends of secondary stems, which in turn grow from a wiry, creeping primary stem. The rosette of some 18-22 leaves somewhat resembles a small green rose. The leaf margins are revolute and finely toothed towards the leaf tip, which ends in a short mucronate point. The leaf midrib is prominent. Leaves growing on the primary stem are small and scale-like, while the basal leaves on the secondary stems are also very small. It occurs in short grassland in open woodland, occasionally in forests, heaths, sand dunes and chalk grassland, and on grassy rock ledges and tree trunks.<ref name="rbge">{{cite web|url=http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/bbs/Activities/mosses/Rhodobryum%20roseum.pdf|date=2010-02-01|title=Bryales | Rhodobryum roseum |access-date=2018-04-14}}</ref>

==Uses==
This is a useful medicinal species. Extracts such as [[ursolic acid]], [[flavonoids]] and [[alkaloids]] have been used in cardiac and other medical research. Mosses show great diversity in morphology and anatomy of their gametophytes and sporophytes. Because of their small sizes it is difficult differentiating between ''Rhodobryum roseum'' and its [[adulterants]] by traditional methods. In particular ''Rhodobryum roseum'' is often confused with ''[[Rhodobryum ontariense]]'', and ''[[Plagiomnium actum]]'', ''[[Plagiomnium maximoviczii]]'' and ''[[Mnium laevinarve]]'' from closely allied taxa.<ref name="plos">{{Cite journal|title=Classification and identification of Rhodobryum roseum Limpr. and its adulterants based on fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and chemometrics|journal=PLOS ONE|volume=12|issue=2|article-number=e0172359|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0172359|pmid=28207900|year=2017|last1=Cao|first1=Zhen|last2=Wang|first2=Zhenjie|last3=Shang|first3=Zhonglin|last4=Zhao|first4=Jiancheng|pmc=5313229|doi-access=free|bibcode=2017PLoSO..1272359C }}</ref>
